mainTopic: How much of the hand must be washed for חולין, for תרומה, and for קידוש ידים ורגלים in the מקדש; what counts as a חציצה; and רב's rule that one morning washing can last all day with a condition.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about how far up the hand water must reach for נטילת ידים, and how far for קידוש ידים ורגלים in the מקדש. It also teaches that anything that is a חציצה for טבילה is also a חציצה for both kinds of washing. רב, שמואל and רב ששת then point to their fingers and disagree about where 'the joint' is. רב gives one limit for חולין and a farther one for תרומה. שמואל uses the farther joint for both, and רב ששת uses the closer joint for both. בר הדיא reports that רבי אמי followed the strict view for both. The גמרא rules out the idea that רבי אמי was strict only because he was a כהן, since רבי מיישא, a לוי, said the same. Finally, רב teaches that one may wash in the morning with a condition that it counts all day. A story about רבי אבינא begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How far to wash, and what blocks the water
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: in the מקדש, hands and feet are washed up to the joint, and anything that is a חציצה for טבילה is also a חציצה for washing hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: [For חולין one washes] until the joint. Sanctifying the hands and feet in the מקדש is until the joint. Anything that blocks the water in immersing the body also blocks it in washing hands for חולין and in sanctifying hands and feet in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that started just before this. It tells us how much of the hand must get water, and what counts as a barrier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate washings here: regular נטילת ידים before eating חולין, and קידוש ידים ורגלים done by the כהנים before the עבודה. Each has a 'joint' that marks the end of the area to be washed. The rules of חציצה from טבילה in a מקוה carry over to both washings.

keyTerms.meaning: Until the joint: the point on the hand up to which water must reach
The washing of hands and feet that כהנים do before the Temple service
Interposes; blocks the water from touching the skin (a חציצה)
Immersion of the whole body in a מקוה
Ritual washing of the hands before eating bread
Ordinary food that is not holy

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'joints' here. The one for regular eating is on the fingers. The one for the מקדש is farther up, where the palm meets the wrist.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that whatever is a חציצה for טבילה is also a חציצה for נטילת ידים is the basis for why rings, dirt and the like must be removed before washing.

phrases.english: Sanctifying the hands and feet in the Temple —

phrases.notes: This is a different joint, farther up, where the palm meets the wrist.

phrases.english: interposes in washing the hands for non-sacred food,
and in sanctifying the hands and feet in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing in the מקדש goes up to the wrist joint. Whatever is a חציצה for טבילה is also a חציצה for נטילת ידים and for קידוש ידים ורגלים.

steps.title: רב: different joints for חולין and for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב, pointing to his fingers, says one joint is the limit for חולין and a farther joint is the limit for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: until here for חולין, until there for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the ברייתא's 'until the joint' by pointing on his own hand. He says the washing for חולין stops at one place, and for תרומה it goes a bit farther.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב makes a difference between the two kinds of food. For חולין, washing up to the middle finger joint is enough. For תרומה, which is holier, one must wash up to the knuckles where the fingers meet the palm.

keyTerms.meaning: Until here: said while pointing to a spot on the hand
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן; it needs more care with טהרה

phrases.notes: He was pointing on his fingers as he said this; here means the middle joint of the fingers.
This here is farther up, where the fingers meet the palm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'joint' mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For חולין one washes to the middle finger joint; for תרומה one washes to where the fingers meet the palm.

steps.title: שמואל: the farther joint for both
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says one place applies to both חולין and תרומה, and it is the stricter, farther joint.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: until here for both חולין and תרומה, to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. He says there is just one limit for both kinds of food, and it is the stricter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had two different limits. שמואל uses one limit for everything and sets it at the farther joint. So even for regular bread, one washes up to where the fingers meet the palm.

keyTerms.meaning: Both for חולין and for תרומה; the same rule for both
In the strict direction

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן בֵּין לְחוּלִּין בֵּין לִתְרוּמָה,
phrases.english: Until here, both for non-sacred food and for teruma,

phrases.notes: He means he pointed to the farther joint, רב's limit for תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עַד כָּאן בֵּין לְחוּלִּין בֵּין לִתְרוּמָה לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב and gives one stricter limit for both.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both for חולין and for תרומה, one washes to the farther joint.

steps.title: רב ששת: the closer joint for both
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת also uses one place for both, but it is the more lenient, closer joint.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: until here for both חולין and תרומה, to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a third opinion. He agrees with שמואל that there is one limit for both, but he puts it at the easier spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three views. רב has two limits, שמואל has one strict limit, and רב ששת has one lenient limit. For רב ששת, washing to the middle finger joint is enough even for תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: In the lenient direction

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן בֵּין לְחוּלִּין בֵּין לִתְרוּמָה,
phrases.english: Until here, both for non-sacred food and for teruma,

phrases.notes: He pointed to the closer joint, רב's limit for חולין.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: עַד כָּאן בֵּין לְחוּלִּין בֵּין לִתְרוּמָה לְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third view: one limit, the lenient one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both for חולין and for תרומה, washing to the closer joint is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views: רב has two limits (closer for חולין, farther for תרומה). שמואל uses the farther joint for both. רב ששת uses the closer joint for both.

steps.title: בר הדיא saw רבי אמי follow the strict view
steps.stepSummary: בר הדיא testifies that רבי אמי ruled like שמואל: the farther joint for both חולין and תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר הדיא said: I was standing before רבי אמי, and he said: until here, both for חולין and for תרומה, to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone reports what he saw. It is support for שמואל's strict view from a later sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing it firsthand from רבי אמי adds weight to the strict position. רבי אמי, like שמואל, did not split between חולין and תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: I was standing before him; a firsthand report

phrases.english: I was standing before Rabbi Ami,
both for non-sacred food and for teruma, in the stringent direction.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר בַּר הֶדְיָא: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's strict view with a later sage's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that the farther joint applies to both חולין and תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בר הדיא's firsthand report of רבי אמי's ruling.

steps.title: Not because he was a כהן: a לוי said the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the idea that רבי אמי was strict only because he was a כהן, since רבי מיישא, a לוי, ruled the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say רבי אמי was strict because he is a כהן. רבי מיישא, the grandson of רבי יהושע בן לוי, is a לוי, and he also said: until here, both for חולין and for תרומה, to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops a possible way of brushing off the proof from רבי אמי. It brings a second sage who is not a כהן but ruled the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a כהן, who eats תרומה, washes the strict way for everything so he won't mix up the two kinds of food. That would make רבי אמי's practice a personal habit, not a general rule. But a לוי does not eat תרומה and has no such reason, so רבי מיישא's ruling shows the strict view applies to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: And do not say; blocks a wrong explanation before anyone raises it
Priest; eats תרומה
A לוי; does not eat תרומה
Grandson; literally, son of his son

phrases.english: And do not say that Rabbi Ami
[ruled this way] because he is a priest,
phrases.notes: The worry is that a כהן might be strict on purpose so he never mixes up תרומה and regular food.

phrases.aramaic: בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: the grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
both for non-sacred food and for teruma, in the stringent direction.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא תֵּימָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי מִשּׁוּם דְּכֹהֵן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Protects the proof from רבי אמי against an objection and adds a second supporter.
steps.raayaObject: The strict view applies to everyone, not only כהנים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מיישא, a לוי who does not eat תרומה, ruled the same strict way.
steps.whatToRemember: The strict view (farther joint for both) is backed by רבי אמי and by רבי מיישא. Since a לוי ruled this way, it is a general rule and not only a habit of כהנים.

steps.title: רב: wash in the morning, with a condition, for the whole day
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person may wash his hands in the morning and make a condition that this washing covers him all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A person may wash both his hands in the morning and make a condition that it counts for the entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב teaches that one washing in the morning can be good for the whole day if you make a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you would wash again before each meal, because your hands may have touched something. רב allows one morning washing with a stated condition that it lasts all day. This works as long as the person stays aware and guards his hands.

keyTerms.meaning: In the morning
Makes a condition; states in advance what he intends
The entire day

phrases.aramaic: נוֹטֵל אָדָם אֶת שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו שַׁחֲרִית,
phrases.english: A person may wash both his hands in the morning,
and stipulate with regard to them
phrases.notes: He says up front that this washing should count for his meals later on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: נוֹטֵל אָדָם אֶת שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו שַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic within the laws of נטילת ידים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A morning washing with a stated condition can serve for the whole day.

steps.title: Setting up רבי אבינא's instruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story about what רבי אבינא told the people of a certain place. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבינא said to the people of...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up the next move. The גמרא starts telling what רבי אבינא told a group of people, which will connect to רב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence breaks off here and finishes on the next amud. It opens a story that seems to show רב's rule being used in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of; residents of a place

phrases.english: Rabbi Avina said to the inhabitants of

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story that appears to illustrate רב's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule about one morning washing with a condition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבינא's instruction (continued in the next section).
